note: Reviewed CDB90 match 5, pinned revision e0b35ec4d798cec3bb4e6970c0f6bb7aa69e2f4c. CDB90 (CAA Database of Battles, Version 1990), tidy data maintained by Jeffrey B. Arnold. Original US Army Concepts Analysis Agency data; revised data licensed ODC-BY. Original force designations and strength interpretations are retained with each quantity. Each side is one aggregate force, including any coalition; its total is not allocated among members. Personnel casualties are not deaths. Source estimates and adjudged error margins are not statistical confidence intervals. Equipment and tactical movements are not established by this dataset. Match review: The state heritage office identifies the 27 August 1626 battle and Christian IV's Danish and north German allied army against Catholic-Imperial troops. NDB identifies Tilly. Source forces remain local, including the Danish coalition; no whole force is assigned to the catalogue's Holy Roman Empire participant. Identity review (attacker; original CDB90 name HOLY LEAGUE ARMY): CDB HOLY LEAGUE ARMY is the force under Tilly; the heritage account describes Catholic-Imperial troops. This is a local combined force, not an invented country allocation. Identity review (defender; original CDB90 name DAN ARMY): CDB DAN ARMY includes the king's north German allies identified by the state heritage office; retain the complete source total as a local army.
